terms.definition: A contact force between two surfaces that resists them sliding past each other.
terms.function: Opposes the sliding motion and depends on surface roughness and pressing force.
terms.whereItIs: Between the book and the bench strip beneath it.
terms.whyItMatters: It gives us grip (walking, braking) and costs us energy (heat, wear).

terms.definition: The rule that friction always pushes back against the direction of motion.
terms.whyItMatters: It is why objects slow and stop on their own — friction pulls the other way.
terms.whereItIs: The arrow drawn opposite the book's travel.

terms.definition: How much a surface's texture grabs — rough grips, smooth slides.
terms.whyItMatters: Together with pressing force it sets the size of the friction, from sandpaper-high to ice-near-zero.
terms.whereItIs: The three tiles with different textures along the bench.

terms.definition: The support force pushing back perpendicular to a surface.
terms.whyItMatters: Press harder and the normal force grows — and friction grows right along with it.
